title: Akshay in All Black, Shahid Looking Like a Painting, and Ananya Birla's ₹2.3 Crore Watch: The Night Bollywood Dressed Up
excerpt: The Bollywood Hungama Style Icons Awards 2026 crowned its kings and queens at JW Marriott Juhu — here are the winners, the fashion, and the moments that mattered
body:
There's a night every year where Bollywood stops pretending it doesn't care about fashion and just *commits*. The fourth edition of the Bollywood Hungama Style Icons Summit and Awards was that night — and if you weren't at JW Marriott Juhu on June 25, you missed a red carpet that was essentially a masterclass in how India's biggest stars have learned to dress.

Let's start where the evening ended: with the two men who walked away with the biggest titles of the night.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=uIEJSomwYXM

Akshay and Shahid: The Heavyweight Duo

Akshay Kumar took home The People's Superstar and Style Icon award — and whatever you think about his recent box office choices, the man has never not looked the part. Fresh off the thunderous opening weekend of *Welcome To The Jungle*, Kumar showed up in sharp, minimal tailoring that said exactly what it needed to: I'm the biggest star in the room, and I know it.

Shahid Kapoor, crowned Icon of Indian Cinema, was the evening's other magnetic presence. Kapoor has spent the last year quietly building one of the most interesting second acts in Bollywood — *Cocktail 2* just crossed ₹75 crore — and his red carpet look matched the energy: confident, sculpted, effortlessly editorial.

The Night Belonged to *Main Vaapas Aaunga*

If there was a single film that dominated the awards, it was Imtiaz Ali's sleeper hit. *Main Vaapas Aaunga* swept four major categories — Iconic Film of the Year, Iconic Filmmaker for Ali, Mega Performer of the Year (Female) for Sharvari, and producer Ananya Birla also celebrated the win alongside her own Most Stylish Business Leader honour.

Sharvari, who's been on an extraordinary run between *Main Vaapas Aaunga* and the upcoming *Alpha*, is quickly becoming Bollywood's most in-demand young actress — and the awards room clearly agreed.

The Performers Who Stole the Night

Ayushmann Khurrana picked up Power-Packed Performer of the Year for *Thamma*, while Rajkummar Rao was named Iconic Actor of the Year. Jim Sarbh — who's been phenomenal in *Made In India: The Titan Story* — won Mega Performer of the Year (Male), a richly deserved recognition for an actor who's been consistently brilliant.

Ananya Panday earned Standout Performance of the Year (Female) for *Kesari 2*, a win that feels like the industry formally acknowledging her evolution from star kid to genuine performer. Bhumi Pednekar took Outstanding Performance for *Daldal*, and the special mention for acting excellence went to the eternally underappreciated Kay Kay Menon.

The breakthrough award landed perfectly: Vedang Raina, the fresh face from *Main Vaapas Aaunga*, whose natural screen presence has been one of the year's revelations.

Fashion That Actually Mattered

But let's be honest — at a *style* awards, the clothes are half the story.

Ananya Birla turned the most heads with a pastel-pink bouclé duster coat over a cropped white tank and high-waisted wide-leg denim — red carpet dressing that felt genuinely modern rather than formulaic. The real conversation starter was her wrist: an Audemars Piguet Royal Oak fully set with diamonds, valued at approximately ₹2.3 crore. Casual.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DaCebwEjPYt/

Vaani Kapoor won Most Stylish Haute Stepper and dressed accordingly. Nawazuddin Siddiqui, named Most Stylish Splendid Performer (Male), continues his quiet transformation into one of Bollywood's more interesting fashion stories — the man who built his career on grit and intensity has discovered tailoring, and it suits him.

Milind Soman and Ankita Konwar arrived as the Global Icons — the Ironman couple whose fitness-first aesthetic has made them social media royalty among wellness-obsessed millennials.

The Full Winners List

  • **The People's Superstar and Style Icon** — Akshay Kumar
  • **Icon of Indian Cinema** — Shahid Kapoor
  • **Power-Packed Performer of the Year** — Ayushmann Khurrana (*Thamma*)
  • **Iconic Actor of the Year** — Rajkummar Rao
  • **Mega Performer (Male)** — Jim Sarbh (*Made In India*)
  • **Mega Performer (Female)** — Huma Qureshi
  • **Standout Performance (Female)** — Ananya Panday (*Kesari 2*)
  • **Most Stylish Splendid Performer (Male)** — Nawazuddin Siddiqui
  • **Most Stylish Splendid Performer (Female)** — Rakul Preet Singh
  • **Mega Performer (Female, Popular Choice)** — Sharvari (*Main Vaapas Aaunga*)
  • **Iconic Film of the Year** — *Main Vaapas Aaunga*
  • **Iconic Filmmaker** — Imtiaz Ali
  • **Outstanding Performance (Male)** — Arshad Warsi
  • **Outstanding Performance (Female)** — Bhumi Pednekar (*Daldal*)
  • **Breakthrough Performance** — Vedang Raina
  • **Timeless Screen Icon** — Boman Irani
  • **Social Impact Icon** — Sonu Sood
  • **Most Stylish Business Leader** — Ananya Birla
  • **Most Stylish Pan-India Icon** — Pooja Hegde
  • **Most Stylish Pathbreaking Star (Female)** — Manushi Chhillar
  • **Most Stylish Pathbreaking Star (Male)** — Ali Fazal
  • **Inspirational Artist** — Jaideep Ahlawat
  • **Most Stylish Groundbreaking Star** — Rasha Thadani

The Bigger Picture

The BH Style Icons night doubles as an unofficial temperature check on Bollywood's cultural confidence. After years of identity crises — the pandemic, the South Indian cinema dominance narrative, the streaming vs theatrical wars — nights like this feel like an industry that's found its swagger again.

June 2026 has been Bollywood's biggest month in years: *Cocktail 2* at ₹80 crore, *Welcome To The Jungle* crossing ₹100 crore worldwide, *Main Vaapas Aaunga* as the word-of-mouth miracle at ₹65 crore, and *Alpha* opening this Thursday. The stars who showed up at JW Marriott know they're riding a wave — and they dressed like it.

For diaspora audiences watching from abroad, nights like these are a reminder of what Bollywood does better than any other film industry on earth: spectacle, beauty, and the unapologetic celebration of star power.
